mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive, but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 4% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: UNRATE drops below 4%, but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate alongside increasing inflation (CPI) signals tighter monetary policy, negatively impacting equity valuations.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS and CPI both increase, but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Declining housing starts (HOUST) in a late-cycle expansion signals slowing economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: HOUST declines, but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, leading to higher consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: PAYEMS increases, but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns within 5 days.
failure_condition: RSAFS increases by 2%, but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 25% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production (INDPRO) alongside low unemployment (UNRATE) signals strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO increases and UNRATE decreases, but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate in a tightening cycle increases borrowing costs, negatively impacting equity valuations and S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.
